newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-VENTAMONJAKS STATE STAKE SELL-OFF RULES SET.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-VENTAMONJAKS STATE STAKE SELL-OFF RULES SET.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Friday that it has set the rules for the sell-off rules of the state's 26 percent stake in Ventamonjaks, one of the biggest ammonia and chemical cargo terminals in the Baltic.
"The state's 26 percent in the company or 35,010 shares will be sold at a price of 155 lats each," LPA official Liga Priedite told Reuters.
The owners of Ventamonjaks have six weeks to exercise a first right of refusal on the state's share, she added.
The total number of Ventamonjaks shares is 131,444 and their nominal value is 100 lats. It is co-owned by Ventspils municipality and firms Solvalub Ltd, Ventk Co Ltd and Solvtrans.
Ventamonjaks earlier said its 1996 profit was 68,000 lats on net turnover of 14.5 million lats.
It plans a slight cargo turnover increase in 1997 to 1.8 million tonnes against last year's 1.7 million tonnes with a planned profit of 150,000 lats.
